summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with alcoholic cirrhosis and a history of recurrent gastrointestinal bleeding was admitted for weakness, fatigue, and melena. On admission, she had a hemoglobin of 8.1 g/dL and acute kidney injury with creatinine elevated to 1.7 mg/dL, likely due to prerenal causes from chronic blood loss and dehydration. She underwent a capsule endoscopy to evaluate for a small bowel source of bleeding, which did not show active bleeding but results required further outpatient review. Her kidney function improved with albumin infusions and discontinuation of diuretics, with creatinine normalizing to 1.0 mg/dL. She received two units of packed red blood cells during the admission for symptomatic anemia. Her blood pressure remained low but stable, and she did not develop signs of hepatic decompensation. She was discharged home with instructions to hold diuretics until follow-up, continue pantoprazole, monitor for fluid retention, and complete weekly lab monitoring with results faxed to her liver specialist.
problems: Esophageal varices in diseases classified elsewhere, without mention of bleeding
